subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured credential-shaped keys under `skills.entries.<skill>.env` bypass the generic sensitive-name block for the active skill's host run while dangerous host override names and unrelated generic exec inheritance remain blocked?
rationale: The docs and current source support the user's expected host-run env injection, but the repair changes a credential-to-exec security boundary and overlaps the inverse leak tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78528.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit only keys explicitly configured for the active skill to bypass the sensitive-name block, with tests for dangerous-name rejection and unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare every sensitive env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary credential-shaped config env keys are not expected to work.

options.title: Design a new secret contract
options.body: Defer the bypass and define a plugin or SecretRef execution contract for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit only keys explicitly configured for the active skill to bypass the sensitive-name block, with tests for dangerous-name rejection and unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env and SecretRef repair path.
